item.title: One of Portland’s Few Black-Owned Music Venues is Facing Eviction
item.description: The Heights owner claims predatory lease terms left him in default. His landlord says payments were missed even after a rent reduction. by Nolan Parker One of Portland’s few Black-owned music venues is facing eviction from its location in Southeast Portland. The Heights lounge and event space was founded in 2024 by local musician Jermaine Malone. Since then, it’s operated out of a 3,800-square-foot space on SE Foster Road. item.title: Despite DOJ Intervention, Portland Police are Still Killing People in Mental Health Crisis
item.description: A grand jury declined to indict officers who used deadly restraint on a man with schizophrenia in June. His family is weighing legal options. by Courtney Vaughn Teri Johnson never expected justice. item.title: Crows at Night
item.description: by Anonymous Crows are supposed to fall asleep after sundown. By tradition, they gather to squawk the daily news before roosting when daylight dips. item.title: All my other tenants are happy!
item.description: by Anonymous Sorry lady but nobody likes their landlord. In fact, several massive civil conflicts ("revolutions" one might say) have been waged around the world about this matter, regarding which tenants are pretty universally united: rent sucks. If you want people to be happy with your work, maybe you should get a job that helps people rather than exploits them for nothing.

item.title: Bi Gan’s Resurrection Revives 100 Years of Movie-Making for One Long Dream
item.description: Dream logic takes over in the Chinese writer-director’s latest technical marvel. by Dom Sinacola Chinese writer-director Bi Gan believes that filmmaking can capture his wildest dreams.
